items.title: PKR Youth backs UUCA repeal, urges students to speak up for wider reforms
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — PKR Youth today backed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement to repeal the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA), but said the move should pave the way for wider reforms to strengthen university autonomy, academic freedom and student rights. The party’s youth wing also urged students to continue speaking up and acting as a check and balance on the government, despite being part of Anwar’s own party. “To Malaysian students, do not stop speaking up.

items.title: Mara chairman orders SOP review after missing MRSM Alor Gajah students found
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) management has been instructed to review its standard operating procedure (SOP) for taking students to health clinics following the disappearance of two MRSM Alor Gajah students for four days. "Whatever the cause of the two MRSM Alor Gajah students going missing for four days, I have instructed Mara management to review the SOP for taking students to clinics to prevent similar incidents. Following the incident, numerous social media users shared comments regarding the current SOP for bringing MRSM students to clinics for medical treatment.

items.title: Titiwangsa pond dries up during maintenance, rain restores water level
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A pond at Titiwangsa Lake Gardens here appeared to have dried up, sparking public concern after images of the site went viral on social media. A notice issued by Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) also informed the public that maintenance work was underway. Visitor Peaceca Anak Cally, 25, said the dry pond had somewhat affected the scenery and image of Titiwangsa Lake Gardens, one of the city's popular recreational spots.

items.title: Anwar announces special Madani F1 tickets for MyKad holders from RM200
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — Malaysians holding MyKad will be able to attend all three days of Formula 1’s return to Sepang through special Tiket Madani priced from RM200, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today. He said the initiative would give more Malaysians the opportunity to experience Formula 1 in person when the race returns to Sepang in October. Anwar said the initiative was aimed at giving more Malaysians the chance to experience Formula 1 directly at Sepang.

items.title: Anwar says allocations for Sabah, Sarawak, Kedah and Kelantan increased under Madani govt
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today dismissed claims by certain quarters that the Madani Government is sidelining several states. “Terengganu’s allocation rose from RM6 billion in 2022 to RM8.1 billion this year, as did Perlis, Johor and others. Anwar said the Federal allocation to Sabah had also increased by 35 per cent, from RM13 billion in 2022 to RM17.6 billion in 2026, while Sarawak’s allocation rose from RM10.2 billion in 2022 to RM15.1 billion, an increase of 48 per cent.

items.title: AUKU abolition to be brought to Cabinet on Wednesday, says Anwar
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said the government's proposal to abolish the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) will be tabled at the Cabinet meeting this Wednesday. Earlier in his speech, Anwar announced the government would abolish the Act as part of its broader reform agenda, particularly in response to concerns raised by university students. Anwar said the abolition was among several reforms the government intended to pursue more decisively after initially prioritising political stability, national security and economic growth.

items.title: Tabung Haji RCI: Shipping CEO, directors among seven held by MACC
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A shipping company chief executive officer with a Datuk title is among seven people detained by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to assist investigations into the Tabung Haji (TH) Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI). Also detained were a company director and a former company director, both holding Datuk and Datuk Seri titles respectively, as well as four former senior TH management officers. Only two male suspects — the shipping company CEO and a construction company director with a Datuk title — were remanded.

items.title: Missing three days, found 140km away, back with families but KL police still investigating case of two Alor Gajah MRSM students
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — Two 16-year-old MRSM Alor Gajah students who went missing for three days have been reunited with their families. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the two teenagers were found at about 10.30pm yesterday at Central Market here — nearly 140km away from the Melaka school campus. The students, Siti Nur Aaira Aidi and Nur Aisy Humaira Mohd Saad, were reported missing after a teacher lodged a police report at 10.46pm on August 11.

items.title: South Korean AI chip tycoon appeals record US$666m divorce ruling
items.summary: SEOUL: South Korea's AI chip tycoon has appealed a court ruling ordering him to pay US$666 million to his former wife in the country's largest-ever divorce settlement, his lawyers said Saturday. Chey Tae-won, 65, is the chairman of the SK Group, which owns world-leading memory chipmaker SK hynix – a pillar of South Korea's tech-led economy. Seoul High Court ruled last month that Roh was entitled to a cash payout worth one-third of the couple's marital assets, including Chey's SK shares, citing her family role and support for SK Group activities.

items.title: Anwar denies rift with Zahid, says ties remain good
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today dismissed claims of a strained relationship with Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, saying ties between them remained good at the national level. Anwar, who is also PKR president, described former Umno Youth chief Khairy Jamaluddin's assessment of his relationship with the Umno president as a personal view shaped by a tendency to view politics through conflict. Asked whether his relationship with Zahid remained good at the national level, Anwar replied: "Still good."

items.title: Not all of Umno can be guilty: Pakatan Harapan should not use an overly generic approach – Phar Kim Beng
items.summary: The principle should be straightforward: not all of Umno can be guilty simply because some Umno leaders, office-holders or political appointees may have been implicated in wrongdoing. Investigations must identify particular decisions, particular offices, particular individuals and particular periods. Umno is not one person.

items.title: Teacher in student, mother assault probe released on police bail
items.summary: PASIR MAS: A 54-year-old teacher remanded over the alleged assault of a 14-year-old student and his mother was released on police bail this morning. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Mazlan Hassan said the suspect was released after his three-day remand order expired today. Following the report, police obtained a three-day remand order against the teacher from Aug 13 to Aug 15.

items.title: UK slams Netanyahu over 'Islamic republic of Britain' remark
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Britain on Friday hit back at Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu derisively calling the country an "Islamic republic" in an interview, branding the remarks "completely unacceptable." Netanyahu asked. "Someone once said that the first Islamic republic with nuclear weapons would be the Islamic republic of Britain," he added with a smile.

items.title: Anwar on Tabung Haji RCI findings: ‘RM12b was lost, isn’t that sakau?’
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has stressed that acts of “sakau” (siphoning of funds) did occur in Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), following the loss of billions of ringgit as highlighted in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the institution. “Some people do not like the term ‘sakau’. Meanwhile, the Prime Minister said His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim.

items.title: Melaka MRSM Alor Gajah students sought treatment before being found at Central Market
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The two 16-year-old MRSM Alor Gajah students who were reported missing had sought treatment at a nearby health clinic before they were found at Central Market last night. City police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the pair were found by Alor Gajah district police personnel about 10.30pm. "Alhamdulillah, police found both Siti Nur Aaira and Nur Aisy Humaira," he said in a Facebook post.

items.title: 19 million US eggs recalled over deadly Salmonella risk
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has said some 19 million eggs that were voluntarily recalled pose a reasonable risk of serious health consequences, including death. Midwest Poultry Services voluntarily recalled the eggs over potential contamination with Salmonella Enteritidis on July 22. In all, 1,589,577 dozen eggs were covered by the recall, and included both white shell eggs and brown cage free shell eggs under a variety of brand names.

items.title: Anwar announces repeal of Universities and University Colleges Act, after students push for greater freedom
items.summary: AYER KEROH, Aug 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today announced that the government will repeal the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA), following continued calls from students for greater freedom. Anwar, who is also PKR president, said the decision came after several amendments to the Act failed to address all concerns raised by university students, local media reported. The 2024 amendments also shifted disciplinary decisions involving public university students from the vice-chancellor to Student Disciplinary Committees through amendments to Section 16B.

items.title: Rohingya father, two young sons die in Bagan Serai house fire
items.summary: Perak Fire and Rescue Department director Datuk Sayani Saidon said the department received an emergency call at 5.17am before firefighters were dispatched to the scene. He said two fire engines and an Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) vehicle arrived at the house at 5.30am. She said firefighters immediately launched a search and rescue operation and found the three victims inside an empty room that was on fire.

items.title: Woman rescued by public after falling from Darul Hana Bridge in Kuching
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 15 — A woman was rescued by members of the public after falling from the Darul Hana Bridge at Kuching Waterfront here yesterday evening. “Initial investigations found that the incident was related to a personal issue — however, investigations are ongoing to determine the root cause of the incident. Those with information related to the incident may contact the Kuching district police headquarters at 082-244444 or the investigating officer, Insp Logeswara, at 018-2914239.

items.title: Sibu latest to record unhealthy API as nine Sarawak areas affected
items.summary: Meanwhile, 46 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while 13 areas recorded good air quality. API readings from 0 to 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and readings above 300 are hazardous. API data is released hourly from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide.

items.title: Anwar announces abolition of Universities and University Colleges Act
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today announced that his government would abolish the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (Act 30). The PKR president said that although several amendments had previously been made, some matters remained unsatisfactory to university students. Also present were PKR and Unity Government leaders, including PKR deputy president Nurul Izzah Anwar, Gabungan Rakyat Sabah chairman Datuk Seri Hajiji Nor and Parti Amanah Negara president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu.

items.title: After Tabung Haji, Anwar says King wants Felda probe next
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 15 — The government will investigate issues involving Felda after completing its probe into alleged misappropriation at Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. “The King told me last week that do not let it end with TH, (but) continue,” Anwar said in his policy speech. “Let the enforcement agencies investigate professionally," he said.

items.title: TNB targets 40,000 mangrove saplings nationwide
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL: Tenaga Nasional Berhad's (TNB) My Brighter Green Initiative (MBGI) 2026 planted 1,500 mangrove saplings at the Chenaam Fishermen's Jetty in Sungai Acheh to restore coastal ecosystems and help protect fisheries resources. TNB Chief Retail Officer Datuk Kamal Arifin A. Rahman said mangrove planting was important in coastal areas as the trees served as breeding grounds for marine life while helping to reduce coastal erosion. "Thank you to TNB for choosing Sungai Acheh and Sungai Chenaam as the location for this year's MBGI mangrove planting project.

items.title: Registration opens for LHDN’s Budget 2027 taxation seminar
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 15 — Registration is now open for the National Taxation Seminar 2026 (Budget 2027), which will provide updates on taxation developments and Budget 2027 proposals through two online sessions on October 14 and 21. In a statement yesterday, the Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia (LHDN) said the seminar was organised in conjunction with the tabling of Budget 2027, scheduled for October 2026. The seminar will be held in two sessions, with Session 1 on October 14 (Wednesday) and Session 2 on October 21 (Wednesday), via Zoom.

items.title: Nine areas in Sarawak record unhealthy API readings as Sibu joins list
items.summary: Meanwhile, 46 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while 13 areas recorded good air quality. API readings between zero and 50 denote good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and above 300 hazardous. Hourly API data is updated from 68 air quality monitoring stations across the nation.

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar to PKR leaders: Being in power does not mean you are the best
items.summary: AYER KEROH: PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim reminded party leaders today that holding government positions did not make them superior to others, urging them to return to the ground and listen to the people's grievances. Listen, make the necessary adjustments and be prepared to change," he said in his policy speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre here. Anwar, who is prime minister, said leaders must listen with a willingness to change rather than merely preparing to respond or argue, as PKR sought to reconnect with voters despite the government's achievements.

items.title: Fallen trees require systematic prevention, says Fire Dept
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Fallen trees are a growing public safety concern, with the Fire and Rescue Department calling for regular safety audits, better data sharing and consistent maintenance to prevent deaths and injuries. He said emergency calls involving fallen trees remained high, at between 4,400 and 5,200 cases annually, with 1,912 incidents recorded in the first six months of this year alone. "Although the number of cases has not consistently increased, fallen trees continue to pose a serious risk to public safety," he said.

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar: Government to step up reform agenda
items.summary: AYER KEROH: PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government would pursue its reform agenda more aggressively. Anwar, who is also Prime Minister, said the government had initially prioritised political stability, national security and economic growth, but believed sufficient progress had been achieved in those areas to allow the administration to move more decisively on reforms. Anwar said several reform measures had already been implemented under his administration, although others would require more time.

items.title: [UPDATED] PKR Congress: There was indeed 'sakau' involving Tabung Haji, says Anwar
items.summary: AYER KEROH: PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said there had been "sakau" (embezzlement) involving Tabung Haji, as detailed in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into the institution. Anwar, who is prime minister, said the pilgrimage fund had suffered RM12 billion in losses. Anwar said His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, had told him that action against corruption should not stop with Tabung Haji, but should also extend to other agencies, including Felda.

items.title: Perlis gets new acting police chief as predecessor moves to Bukit Aman
items.summary: KANGAR, Aug 15 — Perlis deputy police chief SAC Zaihairul Idrus has been appointed as acting state police chief, effective yesterday. The handover ceremony was witnessed by Bukit Aman KDNKA director Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri and held at the Perlis contingent police headquarters (IPK) here yesterday. “Perlis’ position as a state bordering a neighbouring country requires continued cooperation between the Perlis contingent and Bukit Aman to strengthen security in border areas.

items.title: Two dead after powerful 7.7-magnitude quake hits Indonesia
items.summary: JAKARTAL At least two people died after an earthquake of magnitude 7.7 and dozens of aftershocks struck off eastern Indonesia early on Saturday, the authorities said. Tsunami waves of less than 1 metre were recorded in several areas of the Southeast Asian nation. Strong shaking was felt across East Nusa Tenggara, West Nusa Tenggara and parts of South Sulawesi, and residents in several areas reported shaking lasting about one minute, BNPB said.

items.title: From 'normal guy' to killer: Mangione's anger at US insurers
items.summary: Luigi Mangione, 28, was thrust into the spotlight in 2024 after gunning down UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, a father of two, in broad daylight in Manhattan. The case laid bare deep frustration and anger with America's privatised medical system that Mangione said failed him after a back injury. Speculation about Mangione's motives exploded after his dramatic capture in Pennsylvania after a tipster spotted him at a McDonald's.

items.title: PKFZ chairman says Chinese-linked cargo presence alone isn’t evidence of trade fraud, after US report flagging Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — The Port Klang Free Zone (PKFZ) today rejected any suggestion that the presence of Chinese-linked businesses or cargo at its facility is evidence of tariff evasion, following a new US report that places Malaysia among economies facing elevated risks of illegal transshipment. PKFZ chairman Lim Lip Eng said the free zone operated within a regulated customs and trade compliance framework and did not facilitate or endorse false declarations, misrepresentation of origin or circumvention of international trade measures. “PKFZ also welcomes greater scrutiny and stronger enforcement against genuine cases of trade fraud,” Lim said.

items.title: Police confirm body found inside suitcase in Sungai Perak is female
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 15 — Police have confirmed that the body discovered inside a suitcase in Sungai Perak near the Lembah Kuala Kangsar jetty yesterday afternoon is that of a woman. Kuala Kangsar police chief ACP Heisham Harun said preliminary investigations found that the victim is approximately 30 years old, though her identity has yet to be determined. He said police received a call from a man at 3.12pm, reporting that he had found the body in the river near the jetty.

items.title: 7.7-magnitude quake sparks mass evacuation in Indonesia, tsunami warning lifted
items.summary: MAUMERE, Indonesia: A strong 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck off Flores island in eastern Indonesia early Saturday, sending thousands running in panic after authorities issued a tsunami warning. Residents in Nagekeo regency, the area closest to the epicentre, raced for higher ground as the sea retreated – a possible sign of an approaching tsunami, AFP journalists saw. The warning was later lifted.

items.title: Teenager killed, two injured in Kota Tinggi motorcycle crash
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: A 15-year-old boy was killed, while two others sustained injuries in a two-motorcycle crash at the Taman Anggerik junction here last night. District police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said police received a report on the incident involving a Yamaha Ego Scooter and a Kawasaki KR150 motorcycle at 9.05pm. "The two motorcyclists, aged 15 and 26, sustained injuries and are receiving treatment at Kluang Hospital," he said in a statement today.

items.title: 3 family members killed in Pahang house fire [WATCH]
items.summary: KUANTAN: Three family members were killed in a house fire in Desa Mawar, Muadzam Shah, Rompin, early this morning. Pahang Fire and Rescue Department Operations Division assistant director Mohd Salahuddin Isa said an emergency call was received at 4.11am and a team of firefighters was deployed to the scene. He said the fire claimed the lives of a man, his wife and their son, while two other children survived.

items.title: PKR Youth chief urges elected reps to get closer to grassroots ahead of elections
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 15 — Elected leaders need to build strong networks with the community at the grassroots level to ensure that relationships with the people are always maintained, said Angkatan Muda Keadilan (AMK) chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim. “Our presence is important, our narrative is important, our machinery is important, our communication is important. Community relations and our networks at the grassroots level are also important,” he said when wrapping up the debate on the AMK Chief’s Policy Address in conjunction with 2026 AMK National Congress here yesterday.

items.title: Brother checks in on sister at her Sungai Petani shop, only to find her body
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI, Aug 15 — A 77-year-old retired pharmacist went to a shop in Pekan Sungai Lalang here to see his younger sister, only to discover her body after noticing a foul smell coming from the premises. Kuala Muda district police chief Assistant Commissioner Hanyan Ramlan said the man arrived at the shop at about 6pm and became suspicious after detecting the smell from inside. “He then contacted the police for assistance,” Hanyan was quoted as saying by Harian Metro last night.

items.title: Selangor Sultan urges Muslims to show compassion towards all animals, including strays
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 15 — The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, has called on Muslims to always do good and show compassion towards all animals, including strays and wildlife. In line with the Friday sermon titled ‘Ihsan Terhadap Mahkluk Allah SWT’ (compassion towards Allah SWT’s creatures) delivered at mosques throughout Selangor yesterday, His Royal Highness also called on the people to reflect on and understand its contents. Sultan Sharafuddin also said that the relationship between humans and other creatures should always be built on the principles of compassion and responsibility.

items.title: Fuziah says PKR must rebuild after electoral setbacks
items.summary: AYER KEROH: PKR secretary-general Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said the party is entering its national congress wounded by recent electoral setbacks and shifts in political alliances, but its struggle is far from over. Fuziah said several elections had tested PKR's strength, with the party losing political ground in areas it had previously regarded as strongholds, including states it once governed. It has left us hurt," she said.

items.title: Hamzah: BN-Perikatan seat talks must go beyond Melaka, allow room for compromise
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) should work out a nationwide seat allocation formula and be prepared to make concessions if their electoral cooperation is to last, Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin said in an interview with news outlet Free Malaysia Today. The Parti Wawasan president said the two coalitions could not limit negotiations to the coming Melaka election or simply insist on defending seats they currently hold. Hamzah said BN and PN should also consider states where Umno currently holds no state seats if they intend to extend their cooperation nationwide.

items.title: Last embrace: Family mourns teacher killed in LPT2 crash [WATCH]
items.summary: MARANG: "That day, he shook hands with us and hugged us tightly while repeatedly apologising. Those were the words of Mohd Zukri Yaacob, 55, the elder brother of Mohd Fahimi Yaacob, 41, who died in a crash at Km357 of the East Coast Highway 2 (LPT2) near Bukit Besi, Dungun, early yesterday. Zukri said the family was particularly moved by Fahimi's unusual behaviour several days before the crash during a family thanksgiving and tahlil gathering.

items.title: DPM Fadillah recovering well after successful double heart bypass surgery at IJN
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, who is also Energy Transition and Water Transformation Minister (Petra), is recovering well after undergoing successful double coronary artery bypass surgery at the National Heart Institute (IJN) on Wednesday. Following a multidisciplinary team discussion, the medical team determined that coronary artery bypass surgery was the most appropriate course of treatment. “The double bypass surgery was performed on August 12 by IJN Senior Consultant Cardiothoracic Surgeons Prof Datuk Seri Dr Mohamed Ezani Md Taib and Prof Datuk Seri Dr Mond Azhan Yakub, together with Clinical Fellow Cardiothoracic and Vascular Surgery Dr Ahmad Mahir Shamsuddin,” the statement said.

items.title: PKR National Congress begins with Anwar set to outline party direction
items.summary: AYER KEROH: PKR's 2026 National Congress begins here today, with party president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim set to outline its strategic agenda and direction. Held under the theme "Memugar Reformasi, Membina Madani" (Revitalising Reformasi, Building Madani), the two-day congress is expected to provide a platform for the party to strengthen its direction while reaffirming the reformasi principles that underpin PKR's struggle amid the evolving political landscape. Anwar, who is the prime minister, is scheduled to officiate the congress.

items.title: Police believe mother and son killed in Temerloh fuel tanker crash, DNA test underway
items.summary: Temerloh District Police chief ACP Mohd Nasyim Bahron said the driver and passenger of the Perodua Bezza were believed to be a 39-year-old woman and her 12-year-old son, who were pronounced dead at the scene. Mohd Nasyim said the 37-year-old lorry driver, however, managed to escape and sustained only minor injuries. Meanwhile, he said post-mortem examinations on the victims would be conducted today.

items.title: Johor eatery shut down after flies, eggs found in food
items.summary: An MBJB spokesman said the council viewed food safety and cleanliness seriously after inspecting the premises, which scored only 65 per cent, or a Grade C, for cleanliness. Several food handlers had not received anti-typhoid vaccinations and lacked food handler certificates, he said. The cooking area was covered in food waste and grease spills.

items.title: Foreign kidnappers and burglars, woman burnt among major crimes this week
items.summary: They were linked to two previous kidnapping cases in Kuala Lumpur, bringing the gang's involvement to four cases. Police carried out follow-up raids in Kedah, Penang and Kuala Lumpur, arresting another six suspects. Here is a list of the other major crime cases which occurred this week: * Police crippled a suspected burglary gang involving five Chinese nationals following two raids in Sri Petaling and Pudu, Kuala Lumpur on Aug 9.

items.title: Tanker carrying 32,000 litres of fuel crashes into car in Temerloh, two occupants feared burnt
items.summary: KUANTAN, Aug 15 — A fuel tanker carrying 32,000 litres of diesel and petrol crashed into a car at KM9 Jalan Temerloh-Triang yesterday, causing both vehicles to burst into flames, with two occupants of the car feared burnt. Temerloh police chief ACP Mohd Nasyim Bahron said police received information from the public on the incident at about 4.30pm. However, the 37-year-old tanker driver managed to escape and suffered only minor injuries,” he said when contacted.

items.title: Declared as chairs and underwear, but Customs finds 1,240 sex toys in Port Klang container instead
items.summary: The department also detected more than RM40 million worth of contraband in three separate operations involving illegal waste, liquor and cigarettes. Noraidah said the department seized 57 containers of illegal waste in the first half of this year, comprising 351,185kg of metal scrap in 13 containers and 841,552.50kg of plastic scrap in 44 containers. “Checks showed that 13 containers had 351,185kg of metal scrap and 44 containers held 841,552.50kg of plastic scrap.

items.title: Anwar: PKR must remain a mass movement, not just a vehicle to win elections
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) must continue to serve as a mass movement that upholds integrity, social justice, unity and the people’s trust, rather than merely a vehicle for winning elections, its president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Wishing delegates a meaningful PKR National Congress 2026, Anwar said he hoped the gathering would serve as a platform for introspection, allowing the party to assess its achievements and strengthen its resolve to carry forward the Reformasi agenda. The two-day PKR National Congress 2026 begins today at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) in Ayer Keroh, Melaka, under the theme “Memugar Reformasi, Membina Madani” (Revitalising Reformasi, Building Madani).

items.title: #NSTviral: Traffic congestion hits roads leading to Kea Farm in Cameron Highlands [WATCH]
items.summary: View on Threads User ridzzychanduri said: "Cameron Highlands has gone downhill." Another user, fxrish___, wrote: "The traffic jam atmosphere heading to KEA Farm." User iqxazmi said: "This Cameron Highlands is no longer beautiful.

items.title: Higher-than-expected growth on the cards for Malaysia [WATCH]
items.summary: Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid raised his full-year 2026 growth forecast to 5.2 per cent from 4.8 per cent, after the Q2 economic expansion of 6.0 per cent surpassed the 5.8 per cent advanced estimate. Private investment moderated to 4.3 per cent in Q2 from 7.8 per cent in Q1, while private consumption grew 4.8 per cent, from 4.7 per cent in the preceding quarter. Government spending provided additional support, with public consumption and public investment accelerating to 6.3 per cent and 7.6 per cent respectively, from 5.3 per cent and 4.1 per cent in Q1.

items.title: PKR congress opens amid electoral setbacks and reformist departures
items.summary: The party is grappling with the departure of prominent reformist figures, internal dissent and poor results in Sabah, Johor and Negeri Sembilan, with another state election in Melaka looming. I think PKR is at a crossroads especially after losing people like Rafizi and now Izzah taking leave. A year later, both men resigned as MPs and left PKR.

items.title: Fadhlina urges PKR members to focus on ideas instead of exploiting religion
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 14 — Political competition should be based on ideas and the ability to offer the best solutions to the people, rather than exploiting matters of faith for political gain, said Wanita PKR chief Fadhlina Sidek. She said religious issues should be respected and should not be exploited for political gain, particularly during elections. “Do not incite people over matters of faith or exploit religion arbitrarily.

items.title: Health minister warns contractors: Show progress or risk losing MOH projects
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) will not compromise on unreasonable delays in over 1,300 health facility development projects nationwide, and is prepared to terminate the contracts of contractors who fail to show convincing physical progress on-site. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said in a Facebook post today that such action is necessary to ensure planned projects are completed according to requirements so that the public can enjoy the benefits promptly, while also preventing the waste of public funds. Dzulkefly said that the MOH is also collaborating with the JKR, state governments, and utility companies to resolve issues affecting project implementation at the grassroots level.

items.title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain ahead tonight for Selangor, Perak, Johor and four other states, MetMalaysia warns
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain, and strong winds expected to affect seven states until 9pm today. In a statement, MetMalaysia said the affected states are Perak (Bagan Datuk, Muallim, Hilir Perak, and Batang Padang), Terengganu, Pahang, and Johor (Mersing). A similar warning was also issued for Selangor (Sepang, Klang, Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor, and Kuala Langat), Negeri Sembilan (Rembau and Port Dickson), and Melaka (Alor Gajah and Melaka Tengah).

items.title: KTMB adds 124 ETS, EMU Plus services, nearly 39,000 seats for National Day, school holidays
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) is adding 124 services with 38,944 seats for its Electric Train Service (ETS) and Electric Multiple Unit (EMU) Plus services during the upcoming National Day and school holidays. In a statement today, KTMB said 100 additional ETS services, offering 31,600 seats, would operate over 10 days from August 21 to 23, August 28 to 31, and September 4 to 6. Additionally, 24 extra EMU Plus services, offering a total of 7,344 seats, will operate on selected dates from August 21 to September 6, including an extension of services to Bandar Tasik Selatan.

items.title: Free rides are over: LRT3 Shah Alam Line passengers start paying tomorrow
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 14 — After six weeks of enjoying free fares, passengers on the Light Rail Transit 3 (LRT3) Shah Alam Line will start to pay for their rides starting tomorrow (August 15). The public transport operator also informed that passengers can check the fare rates for the Shah Alam Line via the official MyRapid website. “Rapid KL welcomes the public to continue travelling with the Shah Alam Line and make public transport an option for easier, safer and smoother daily travel,” the statement said.

items.title: ‘Extraordinarily rash’: Prosecutor says police officer deliberately chased Ipoh teen before fatal crash
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 14 — The High Court here was told today that the action of a senior police officer chasing a victim at high speed before crashing into him was described as a very dangerous act and showed “extraordinary rashness”. Deputy Public Prosecutor Afzainizam Abdul Aziz in his rebuttal said that DSP Mohd Nazri Abdul Razak’s action of chasing Muhammad Zaharif Affendi Muhd Zamrie at close range was done with the knowledge that the act could result in death. He said the accused was found not slowing down the Perodua Ativa he was driving even after passing a bump in the school area, but instead continued to follow closely before crashing into the victim at an intersection.
